tasks.brief: Write an email to Dr. Raman asking her to put a review of our sepsis order set's antibiotic timing recommendation on the December P&T agenda. Facts: our internal audit of 412 sepsis cases from Jan to Sept found median time to first antibiotic was 74 minutes against the 60-minute target; the order set currently defaults to a pharmacy-verified piperacillin-tazobactam order that adds about 15 minutes of verification; the 2021 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guideline recommends antibiotics within 1 hour for septic shock or high likelihood of sepsis; I'd like 15 minutes on the December 9 agenda.
tasks.draft:
Subject: Request for December P&T Agenda Item – Sepsis Order Set Review

Dear Dr. Raman,

I hope this message finds you well. I am writing to respectfully request that the Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee consider adding a review of our sepsis order set's antibiotic timing recommendation to the agenda for the upcoming December meeting.

As you may know, timely antibiotic administration is a critical component of effective sepsis care. With this in mind, our team conducted an internal audit of 412 sepsis cases from January to September. The audit found that the median time to first antibiotic was 74 minutes, which exceeds our 60-minute target. This is an important finding that we believe warrants the committee's attention.

One contributing factor may be that the order set currently defaults to a pharmacy-verified piperacillin-tazobactam order, which adds approximately 15 minutes of verification time. Additionally, it is worth noting that the 2021 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guideline recommends administering antibiotics within one hour for patients with septic shock or a high likelihood of sepsis.

Given these considerations, I would like to request 15 minutes on the December 9 agenda to present our findings and discuss potential next steps.

Thank you so much for your time and consideration. Please don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions or would like to discuss this further. I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
[Your Name]

tasks.draft:
Hi Priya,

I hope your week is off to a good start! I wanted to take a moment to give you a quick update on where things stand with the volumetric terrain view, as I know you're planning for Thursday's TestFlight build.

Unfortunately, after careful consideration, I don't think the volumetric terrain view will be ready in time for Thursday's build. The main issue is that the Metal compute pass for chunk culling is still dropping frames on the M2 Vision Pro. Our target is 90 fps, but we're currently seeing around 61 fps with 40 chunks visible, which isn't where we need it to be for a good experience.

Given all of this, I'd suggest we target the build on Tuesday, Nov 24 for the volumetric terrain view instead.

Please let me know if you have any questions or if there's anything else I can do to help. Thank you so much for your understanding!

Best,
Alex

tasks.reader: Dr. Anita Rao, the principal investigator who leads the research team and is the writer's direct supervisor, who needs to decide whether to include a contested finding in a grant renewal.
tasks.context: You open this email in your inbox on Tuesday morning, a few days before the internal deadline for locking the evidence section of the renewal application.
tasks.brief: Write an email to Anita telling her I recommend we cite the school-based sleep-intervention effect as 'modest and uncertain' rather than 'effective' in the renewal. Facts: I reviewed 14 studies, only 4 are randomized; pooled effect in the randomized ones is 0.18 SD on attendance, with a confidence interval of 0.02 to 0.34; the two large positive studies both come from the same research group; I need her sign-off by Friday Nov 20.
tasks.draft:
Subject: Recommendation on how we describe the sleep-intervention evidence

Hi Anita,

I hope your week is off to a good start! I wanted to take a moment to reach out regarding the evidence section of our grant renewal, as I know the deadline is approaching and I want to make sure we are all on the same page.

As part of my work on the literature review, I have been carefully looking at the body of evidence on school-based sleep interventions. Overall, I reviewed 14 studies in total. Of these, only 4 are randomized, which is an important consideration when thinking about how much weight we can place on the findings. When I pooled the effect from the randomized studies, I found an effect of 0.18 SD on attendance, with a confidence interval ranging from 0.02 to 0.34. It is also worth noting that the two large positive studies both come from the same research group, which may be relevant when considering the strength of the evidence.

Given all of this, I would like to recommend that we describe the effect in the renewal as "modest and uncertain" rather than "effective." I believe this wording more accurately reflects what the evidence can support and will help us avoid overstating our claims.

Could you please let me know whether you are comfortable with this approach by Friday, November 20? Your sign-off would be greatly appreciated so that we can finalize the section in time.

Please don't hesitate to reach out if you would like to discuss any of this further or if you have any questions. Thank you so much for your time and consideration!

Best regards,
[Name]

tasks.draft:
Subject: Update on the Flood Viewer Launch Timeline

Hi Dana,

I hope your week is off to a great start! I wanted to reach out and provide you with an update on the status of the Cesium flood viewer, as I know the upcoming launch is important to your team and to the public.

After carefully reviewing where things stand, I regret to inform you that the viewer will unfortunately not be ready for the planned November 20 launch. I'd like to take a moment to explain the situation and share what I'm proposing as a path forward.

The main issue is performance. The LiDAR point cloud is 2.1 GB, and on a typical laptop it currently takes about 14 seconds to load. Our target is under 5 seconds, and I don't feel comfortable launching to the public until we reach it. To address this, I'm converting the data to 3D Tiles, which uses a tiled, level-of-detail structure so that the viewer only loads what is needed at any given time.

In terms of progress, the first converted tiles are already in staging, and I expect the full conversion to finish on November 25. 

Given all of this, I would like to propose a new launch date of December 4. In order to move forward, I would need you to confirm the December 4 date by Thursday, ahead of the go/no-go call.

Please don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions or would like to discuss this further. Thank you so much for your understanding and flexibility, and I look forward to hearing from you!

Best regards,
[Your name]
